Hon'ble Rajeev Singh,J.
1.
It is evident from the counter affidavit that notice has already been served upon private respondent, however, none appears on his behalf.
Therefore, the matter is being proceeded for final disposal.

2. Heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

The present appeal has been filed for quashing the impugned order dated 18.11.2022 passed by learned Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Lucknow in Bail Application No.9749/2022 arising out of Case Crime No.419/2022 under Sections 323, 376, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)(V) of SC/ST Act,
Police Station- P.G.I., District- Lucknow.

sentences.text: 1 4. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that appellant was falsely implicated in the present case as he performed some painting work at the house of victim but when he asked money for the aforesaid work then the F.I.R. of case in question was lodged.
He further submitted that the name of appellant is mentioned in the case diary as Rajiv @ Abdul but he never informed that his nick name is Abdul as his name is Rajiv @ Atul Bajpai.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that during the course of investigation, statement of victim was recorded under Sections 161 as well as 164 Cr.P.C. and as per the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., on 18.07.2022, on 11:00 PM, victim was called in a temple from where she was taken to house of appellant where his parents were not present, thereafter, appellant started skirmish with her in the drunken condition, tore her clothes and committed rape and when she tried to inform her relatives, then appellant and her father took her mobile phone and confined her in a room, anyhow, she saved herself by escaping through window.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that in the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she developed a case stating that about three months ago, when she was alone at her house, the appellant shot a video of her while she was taking bath and threatened her that if she did not make physical relations with him, he will make the aforesaid video viral on the social media, thereafter, under compulsion, she made physical relation with the appellant.

She also stated that appellant had beaten her, bitten on her hand and pressed her neck and given blow on her head,
thereafter, victim was admitted in the hospital.

He further submitted that the victim is a 32 years old major and prudent lady, therefore, such contradiction in her statements reveals that no such incident was taken place but the charge sheet was filed by the Investigating Officer in the most mechanical manner without investigating the contents of statements of victim recorded under Sections 161 as well as 164 Cr.P.C.

He further submitted that trial court also failed to consider evidences available on record in the correct perspective, therefore, the impugned order is liable to be set aside and appellant may be enlarged on bail.
7.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer of appellant and submitted that the victim has supported the prosecution version but he did not dispute this fact that there are contradiction in the statements of victim recorded under Sections 161 as well as 164 Cr.P.C.
8.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the appellant, learned A.G.A. and going through the contents of appeal, statements of victim recorded under Sections 161 as well as 164 Cr.P.C as well as other relevant documents; it is evident that there are major contradiction in the prosecution story, contents of F.I.R. and statements of victim recorded under Sections 161 as well as 164 Cr.P.C, as in the case diary, name of appellant is mentioned asRajiv @ Abdul but his name is Rajiv @ Atul Bajpai but no explanation has been given, as to why, the name of appellant has been mentioned in the case diary as Rajiv @ Abdul.

In such circumstances, this Court is of the view that the trial court failed to consider the aforesaid aspects, hence, the aforesaid impugned order is liable to be set aside and appellant is entitled to be released on bail.

9. Resultantly, in the above facts and circumstances of the case, the trial of the case is not likely to be concluded in near future, hence, the present appeal has substance, and it is accordingly allowed, and Rajveer Alias Atul Bajpai vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: the impugned order dated 18.11.2022 passed by learned Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Lucknow is hereby set aside.

10. Let the appellant- Rajveer Alias Atul Bajpai involved in the aforementioned crime be released on bail, on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned, with the following conditions:-
(i) The appellant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he will not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The appellant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through their counsel.

In case of his absence, without sufficient cause,
the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the appellant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence, proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation

,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
(iv) The appellant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the appellant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
